findings.description: The consuming formulas' exact algebraic shape and row-isolation are pinned by code+tests but never stated by SHEET-FORMULA-005. The EARS text only says '...the live post-tax Est. Unrealized Tax / Net Unrealized formulas that multiply it evaluate numerically...' — it names the formulas abstractly. The real code fixes them precisely: `est_tax = Cell::Formula("={G}*{H}")` and `net_unreal = Cell::Formula("={G}*(1-{H})")` (lib.rs lines 568-569), each built from `cell_ref('G', r)`/`cell_ref('H', r)` for the SAME row r — an anti-cross-row-leak discipline that the sibling test `per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header` explicitly pins for the analogous Market-Value/Unrealized-P&L columns (asserting a formula on row r never contains any OTHER row's E{ro}/B{ro}), and which by identical construction applies to I/J. All three B-runs (B1 SHEET-POS-EST-RATE-005, B2 TAXRATE-06/07/08, B3 item 4) independently reconstruct exactly `=G{r}*H{r}` / `=G{r}*(1-H{r})` plus the own-row-only constraint — high B-agreement on a concrete invariant the EARS text never commits to.

Degraded/absent-rate handling is a real, code-pinned behavior with no trace in SHEET-FORMULA-005. When a symbol has no entry in `effective_rates`, line 585 writes `eff_rate.map(fmt_ppm).unwrap_or_default()` — an empty-string `Cell::Value`, never `"0.0000%"`, never an error marker, never a formula. The EARS text is scoped entirely to the populated-cell case ('so Sheets parses it as a number... e.g. a %-suffixed value') and says nothing about what happens when no rate is available. All three B-runs surface this independently (B1 SHEET-POS-EST-RATE-003/007, B2 TAXRATE-04, B3 item 5), with B1 and B3 further noting the resulting formula-evaluation consequence (blank H is coerced to 0 by Sheets, so Est. Unrealized Tax evaluates to 0 and Net Unrealized falls back to the pre-tax P&L) — a chained consequence the spec text never addresses at all.

The percent string's precision is fixed by the code to exactly 4 zero-padded decimal digits, a constant the EARS never states and all three A-sketches independently guessed wrong. `fmt_ppm` (lib.rs lines 497-505) formats as `"{sign}{whole}.{frac:04}%"` — e.g. `Ppm(150_000)` -> `"15.0000%"` (doc-pinned exact example at line 496). SHEET-FORMULA-005 gives no precision requirement — its own example ('a `%`-suffixed value') is generic. All three A-outputs (A1, A2, A3) independently invented a 2-decimal `"{:02}"` / `"0.00%"` pattern instead — unanimous among A-runs, but unanimously divergent from the real 4-digit constant, and (per audit protocol) not eligible as an A-finding since it isn't traceable to spec text; it is however clean confirmatory evidence that this precision is a real, non-obvious, code-side-only constant. All three B-runs correctly recovered the real 4-digit pattern from the code.

The Est. Tax Rate cell's structural typing as an engine `Cell::Value` (vs `Cell::Formula`), part of the crate-wide `Cell` enum with `is_formula()`/`text()` accessors and directly test-pinned by `live_price_columns_are_formulas_others_are_values`, is a concrete representational commitment the EARS text doesn't itself require (it requires the *outcome* — Sheets parses it numerically — not this specific internal value/formula split). Weak/architectural: largely implied by, and consistent with, the EARS text's substance rather than contradicting it, so ranked last.

notes: The EARS text and the real code's own doc comment on `batch_update_view` (lib.rs lines 439-445) are near-verbatim of each other ('a percent-typed userEnteredValue... a percent-suffixed string such as \"20.0000%\"... NOT a forced string/stringValue'), so the CORE requirement (percent-typed value, not text) is BD-coherent — no drift there. Where the three A-direction sketches disagree most (interpretation of the actual Sheets write mechanism: A1/A3 build numeric `CellData{number_value, NumberFormat::PERCENT}` directly; A2 instead writes a formatted string via `values.update`+`USER_ENTERED`, arguing that's what 'Sheets parses it' implies) is a real ambiguity the EARS text leaves open — but it doesn't rise to a scoreable A-finding because the real `sheets-view` code doesn't resolve it either: it only formats a plain Rust String (`Cell::Value`) and *documents* (never implements or tests, in these two files) the 'written as userEnteredValue not stringValue' obligation as a contract for `runtime`'s (unseen) implementation. So this axis is genuinely unresolved on both sides rather than a code-side behavior the audit can pin — I flagged it here rather than promoting it to a finding. A-agreement is 'medium': all three concur on the top-level goal and (coincidentally, wrongly) on a 2-decimal precision assumption, but split 2-1 on rate sign/type (A2/A3 signed i32 vs A1 unsigned u32 — note A2/A3's signed choice actually matches real `Ppm`'s sign handling), 2-1 on absence handling (A2/A3 add `Option<T>`->blank matching real `unwrap_or_default()`, A1 has no absence path at all), and 2-1 (different composition) on the write-mechanism interpretation above. B-agreement is 'high': B1/B2/B3 converge almost word-for-word on the `Cell::Value` typing, the exact 4-digit `fmt_ppm` format, the empty-string degraded case, the `userEnteredValue`-not-`stringValue` contract, the exact `=G*H`/`=G*(1-H)` formulas with own-row-only referencing, and the `/100 -> [0,1]` fraction invariant tested by `est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply`.
